targetText: Let us now consider the total movement, M ; C ... P ... C' ; M', or, M ; C<LMP ... P ... C' (C + c) ; M' (M + m), its more expanded form. Capital here appears as a value which goes through a series of interconnected, interdependent transformations, a series of metamorphoses which form just as many phases, or stages, of the process as a whole. Two of these phases belong in the sphere of circulation, one of them in that of production. In each one of these phases capital-value has a different form for which there is a correspondingly different, special function. Within this movement the advanced value does not only preserve itself but grows, increases in magnitude. Finally, in the concluding stage, it returns to the same form which it had at the beginning of the process as a whole. This process as a whole constitutes therefore the process of moving in circuits.
explanation: Capital is a self-expanding value moving through interconnected stages: it starts as money, transforms into productive elements, emerges as commodities, and returns as more money. The circuit as a whole is what makes capital "capital".
